overview: **Studying undergraduate (UG) engineering in France is** an attractive option for **international students** who are seeking quality technical education, practical training and the chance to build an international career.
France has ****engineering programmes**** in **mechanical engineering, computer science, aerospace, civil engineering, electrical engineering, robotics** and many other specializations.
**Edu Hawk worldwide** study abroad guidance helps students to explore these opportunities and know about the requirements involved in pursuing education abroad.

sections.title: 8. Engineering Accreditation and Recognition in France**

items: One of the most important factors when choosing an engineering school is ****engineering accreditation in France**.**

The ****Commission des titres d’ingénieur (CTI)**** accredits French engineering programs that comply with its standards and the right to award the French *diplôme d’ingénieur* to their establishments. This qualification usually requires five years of higher education and a master's level grade.
Students should: before enrolling
* - Check the exact qualification awarded.
* - If you are looking for a French engineering diploma, check **CTI accreditation**.
* - Verify that the course is recognized for further studies.
* - Check any rules on professional registration or recognition for the country they want to work in.

sections.title: 9. Salaries and Job Opportunities after Engineering UG in France**

items: Engineering graduates in France may work in France or abroad, depending on their qualification, language skills, experience and work authorization.
**Potential engineering career opportunities** include:
* - Design or mechanical engineer.
* - Computer engineer or software developer.
* - Electronics / Electrical engineer.
* - Civil engineering technician or graduate engineer, depending on the position.
* - Aerospace or manufacturing engineering.
* - Expert in robotics and automation.
* - Analyst in energy and sustainability.
* - Engineer Production or Quality Assurance Engineer.

**Salary expectations:** Salary varies widely according to specialization, location, employer, qualification and experience. A three year Bachelor's graduate and a graduate with a **engineering diploma recognized by CTI** could be eligible for different roles

sections.title: 10. Documents Required to Pursue Undergraduate Engineering in France**

items: Prepare the following ****documents required for engineering admission in France**** as per the requirements of the selected institution:
* - Passport valid.
* - **Marksheet of Class 10 and Class 12.**
* - Secondary school leaving certificate;
* - **Results of language proficiency** (if applicable).
* - **Letter of motivation (statement of purpose).
* - CV available on request.
* - Letters of recommendation, if necessary.
* - Application form and applicable application-fee receipt.
* - Certified translations of documents not accepted in the original language .
* - Other documents requested by the school or admissions platform.
Upon admission, you may also have to present documents for **French student visa processing**, accommodation, financial proof and final enrollment

sections.title: 11. Frequently Asked Questions on B.Sc. Engineering in France**

items: **Q1. Is it possible for Indian students to pursue undergraduate engineering in France?**
Yes. **Indian students can do undergraduate engineering in France** by applying to eligible bachelors and engineering-school programs if they meet the academic, language and application requirements.
**Q2. How long does it take to study undergraduate engineering in France?**
Typical engineering bachelor’s degrees take three years. The traditional **French engineering school route** typically takes five years after high school.
**Q3. Do engineering courses in France teach in English?**

**Many engineering programs in France are taught in English**, including some international bachelor’s degree programs. French is used in many traditional engineering pathways so students should check the language of instruction carefully.
Q4. What is the cost of undergraduate engineering in France?

**Tuition fees for engineering in France** vary depending on the school and the degree. The advertised differentiated tuition for non-EU students at the bachelor’s level in covered public institutions for 2026-2027 is €2,902 per year, but particular engineering programs can set different tuition or offer exemptions.
**Q5. What are the things a student should look for before selecting an engineering university in France?

Check the exact degree awarded, **CTI accreditation** if applicable, language of instruction, eligibility criteria, tuition fees, living costs, application deadlines and career or further-study options.
